answer.rationale: Negotiating terms with the incumbent leverages memory_c4's proof that benchmark-driven renegotiation at renewal recovers margin, while using the low-cost vendor's quote as a pressure point. Memory_c1 confirms that maintaining the incumbent preserves integration stability—critical at 94% capacity with no buffer, where any transition risk is unacceptable. Switching vendors (memory_c2) meets the 18% mandate but introduces delivery risk; a standard negotiation experiment offers a controlled path to cost reduction without increasing operational exposure. The fallback remains switching if negotiation fails within the 14-day window.
